headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty crashed as foreign investors sold stocks en-masse; market closed today for Gandhi Jayanti

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Aggressive selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in the Indian equity market
Rising global crude oil prices with Brent crude nearing $103 per barrel
Concerns over surging US Treasury yields and hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve
Significant foreign exchange losses for Indian banks following RBI position curbs
whatHappening: The Sensex hit a fresh 52-week low after dropping over 570 points in the last session
Indian benchmark indices recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years
The government imposed a 1,000-quintal sugar stock limit for dealers ahead of the festive season
Scions of the INOX Group have filed for two separate IPOs worth ₹10,000 crore each
summary: Indian markets are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti following a sharp decline where the Sensex hit a 52-week low. Heavy foreign investor selling and rising Brent crude prices, now near $103, have driven the longest weekly losing streak in 25 years. Meanwhile, INOX Group scions have filed for major IPOs as the government tightens sugar stock limits.
